title: Direct ENIT: An easy and reliable tool for gRNA efficacy verification by tracking induced chromosomal translocation
author: Lomov, Viushkov, et al.
materials: 1.48 h after transfection detach the cells from a culture plate with 300 µl of 0.05% trypsin solution. Thoroughly resuspended cells in 2 ml DMEM, containing 10% FBS, to inactivate trypsin.2.For each PCR reaction, transfer 200 µl cell suspension to a sterile PCR tube (10,000—50,000 cells). Pellet cells by centrifugation, for 2 min at 1000 rcf, and discard the supernatant.NOTE: Optionally, the pellet can be washed with 1 × PBS, followed by a second centrifugation of the cell suspension using the same centrifugation parameters described above.All subsequent sample manipulations should be performed in a PCR hood to avoid contamination.3.Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 µl proteinase K solution (0.1 mg/ml), in 2 × PCR buffer supplied with DNA polymerase.4.Place the samples in a thermocycler, with pre-heated lid, for 15 min at 60 °C, followed by 3 min at 95 °C.5.To perform the first round of nested PCR, add DNA polymerase, the outer primers, dNTPs, and deionized water to the cell suspension to obtain a final volume of 20 µl. Use the reagent concentrations recommended by the DNA Polymerase manufacturer. Return the PCR tubes to the thermocycler, and perform the first round of nested PCR. The reaction conditions may vary depending on specific primer designs and amplicon sizes. We recommend using at least 1 min for primer annealing and running 20 cycles.6.Prepare two sets of PCR tubes: one containing 156 µl deionized water and one containing 16 µl the second-round PCR mixture, including DNA Polymerase, inner primers, PCR buffer, and dNTPs. Use the reagent concentrations recommended by the DNA Polymerase manufacturer to perform a 20-µl reaction. Add a 4 µl aliquot of the first-round PCR product to the tube containing 156 µl water, mix thoroughly by pipetting the mixture repeatedly and transfer 4 µl diluted sample into the second tube containing the prepared 16 µl PCR mixture; use one filter tip for this procedure to avoid product loss and contamination. Thus, the final second-round reaction mix contains the 200-fold diluted product of the first-round PCR reaction. Thermocycling conditions should be determined based on primer design and the resulting amplicon size; however, we recommend using at least 1 min for primer annealing and running 25 cycles.7.Analyze the second-round PCR products by agarose gel electrophoresis. The PCR reaction performed using cells without translocations should be included as a negative control. The presence of amplicons at the expected length will indicate the successful rearrangement of the targeted loci and the sufficient performance of the tested gRNA.

steps.title: Cell transfection
steps.instruction: Prepare cells and co‑transfect Cas9 plasmid with a pre‑validated gRNA plasmid and the test gRNA plasmid.

substeps.instruction: 1.24 h before transfection, passage HeLa cells (or any suitable line) into a 6‑well plate; optionally change to antibiotic‑ and serum‑free medium (e.g., Opti‑MEM™) 3 h before transfection to improve efficiency.
When cells reach ~70 %–80 % confluency, co‑transfect them with the Cas9‑expressing plasmid and the two gRNA plasmids using the protocol for the chosen transfection reagent.
Add equal amounts of each plasmid so that the total DNA per well is ≈3 µg.
Use 6 µl TurboFect™ Transfection Reagent per well (or any preferred reagent/system).
Include a non‑transfected well as a negative control.

steps.title: Direct nested PCR (nested)
steps.instruction: Lyse cells, perform first‑round PCR, dilute product, and run second‑round nested PCR, then analyse by gel electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: 1.48 h after transfection, detach cells with 300 µl of 0.05 % trypsin solution; immediately resuspend the cells in 2 ml DMEM containing 10 % FBS to inactivate trypsin.

Transfer 200 µl of the suspension (≈10 000–50 000 cells) to a sterile PCR tube, centrifuge 2 min at 1000 rcf, discard supernatant. (Optional: wash pellet with 1 × PBS and repeat centrifugation under the same conditions.) Perform all subsequent steps in a PCR hood.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 µl proteinase K solution (0.1 mg/ml) prepared in 2 × PCR buffer supplied with the DNA polymerase.
Place the tube in a thermocycler with a pre‑heated lid: 15 min at 60 °C, then 3 min at 95 °C.

Add DNA polymerase, outer (first‑round) primers, dNTPs, and deionized water to reach a final volume of 20 µl (use the concentrations recommended by the polymerase manufacturer). Run the first‑round PCR using at least 1 min annealing per cycle and 20 cycles (adjust as needed for amplicon size).

Prepare two new tubes: one containing 156 µl deionized water, the other containing 16 µl of second‑round PCR mix (DNA polymerase, inner primers, PCR buffer, dNTPs) for a 20 µl reaction. Add 4 µl of the first‑round product to the 156 µl water, mix, then transfer 4 µl of this 200‑fold diluted mixture into the 16 µl second‑round mix (use a single filter tip). Run the second‑round PCR with at least 1 min annealing and 25 cycles (conditions depend on primer design and amplicon size).

Analyze the second‑round PCR products by agarose‑gel electrophoresis. Include a negative‑control PCR (cells without induced translocation). The presence of a band at the expected size indicates successful chromosomal translocation and confirms the efficacy of the tested gRNA.
